core_diff_compute|over-limit computation.reason: The test sets MaximumMatrixCells below the comparison's need and expects the baseline's degradation. The candidate's matcher does not use the matrix and publishes an exact, validated alignment.

core_diff_compute|index work is independ.reason: Asserts the baseline's ordered-index accounting (PrimaryIndexWorkConsumed). A candidate matcher reports none; its alignment is exact and validated.

core_diff_compute|an exhausted index bud.reason: Asserts the baseline's index-budget degradation. The candidate is not bound by that budget and publishes an exact, validated alignment, never a refusal.

core_diff_compute|large comparison prese.reason: The same expectation also requires PrimaryIndexWorkConsumed > 0, the baseline's own counter. On the corpus's BPR-0625 comparison every primary candidate publishes the same 20 groups as the baseline.

core_diff_compute|a changed region beyon.reason: The candidate aligns the region exactly where the baseline degrades; the expectation encodes the baseline's limit.

core_diff_compute|an exhausted budget de.reason: Budget-model expectation of the baseline; the candidate's exact alignment validates.

core_diff_compute|[[BPR-1366]] the large.reason: A component call is one restart unit, and the seam assigns line classes in one unit. This is the RFC's Interruption gate, measured as stop-to-return latency, not an alignment.

core_diff_compute|[[BPR-1366]] resumed p.reason: A diff-match-patch pair call has no internal step counting, so a pause cannot land inside it. Judged by the Interruption gate.

core_diff_compute|validator fixture cont.reason: Semantic cleanup joins the two nearby multibyte edits into one span. The edit validates; what it emphasizes is the look-and-judge question of AC06.

core_diff_compute|validator rejects over.reason: The test builds its overlapping fixture from the computed edits and needs two of them. With the joined span there is only one; the validator is unchanged.

core_diff_compute|[[BPR-1366]] a resumed.reason: With dtl as the primary matcher a run resumed after frequent pauses never completes: each slice restarts dtl from the beginning and no slice is long enough to finish it. The inventory timed out after 1,800 s.

core_diff_compute|[[BPR-1366]] a stop re.reason: dtl's run did not pause where the test expects. Seen with the non-terminating resume above.

core_diff_compute|[[BPR-1366]] a stop is.reason: dtl's run overran the stop bound in the same suite run.

core_diff_compute|ambiguous exact moved.reason: Only dtl (c-onp) fails it. Not examined further: c-onp already fails the correctness gate by a crash and by refused (invalid) results.

core_diff_compute|every inserted line is.reason: Only dtl (c-onp) fails it, on the BPR-0719 replica. Not examined further, for the reason above.

application_diff_host|the direct computa.reason: dtl ends the process with an uncaught std::length_error, and refuses comparisons whose results join unequal lines.

application_diff_host|[[BPR-1366]] a pre.reason: The evaluation hook runs the installed Git inside the core's primary step, where a stop cannot kill it. The process shape would run Git in the host and kill it on a stop; stops mode measures that. This test fails on 4 of the 8 installed-Git variants, depending on timing.
